title: Visit for ringing in the ears
what: An ENT doctor finds out where the noise in your ears comes from and checks your hearing. Then they choose treatment or ways to make the noise bother you less.
why: For ringing, noise, or buzzing in one or both ears.
duration: the visit usually takes 30 to 60 minutes; a hearing test takes about 20 minutes
tell_doctor: When the noise started and in which ear
If there was a loud sound, an injury, or a cold
If you have hearing loss or dizziness
If you have high blood pressure

prepare.title: Notes
prepare.text: Write down when the noise is worse and what helps.

prepare.title: Loud sounds
prepare.text: The day before the hearing test, avoid loud music and noise.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Bring a list of all your medicines. Some affect hearing.

steps: The doctor asks about the noise
Your hearing is tested in a soundproof booth
If needed, an MRI or blood tests are ordered
The doctor explains the plan and how to live with the noise
feel: The exam and tests do not hurt
In the booth, you need to focus on quiet sounds
after: Avoid loud sounds and use earplugs in noisy places
Background sound at night may help you fall asleep
Come back as your doctor plans
red_flags: Noise that came on suddenly with hearing loss: see a doctor within a day
Noise with severe dizziness and vomiting
A pulsing noise in one ear
Weakness in an arm or the face, or trouble speaking: call emergency services

faq.a: Sometimes it goes away, sometimes it stays. There are ways to make it less noticeable.

faq.q: Can stress cause ringing in the ears?
faq.a: Stress and lack of sleep often make it worse. But the cause should be found by a doctor.

reminders.text: Visit for ringing in the ears tomorrow. Bring your list of medicines and avoid loud music.
